title: Queued Linger Cohorts and KV Rejuvenation to Reduce Starvation in Continuous Batching
author: Ananya Rao
release_notes: Introduces cohorted linger windows, TTL-based KV rejuvenation hints, and scheduler soft-reservations to reduce starvation for short/latency-sensitive requests; p99 improved in KV-heavy traces with minimal throughput impact.
description:
Motivation: We observed recurring p99 tail spikes for short, KV-heavy requests during sustained continuous-batching workloads. Root cause analysis showed that global linger thresholds and monolithic KV pin lifetimes allowed large, long-running batches to monopolize slots and pin KV entries, starving short requests and causing timeouts.

This PR introduces a multi-pronged approach:
1) Cohorted linger windows: linger timeout is dynamically bucketed by request cohort (inferred from route/request-size/tenant hints) so short/interactive cohorts get lower linger, while background cohorts can tolerate larger coalescing.
2) Soft-reservations and min-service quotas: the scheduler guarantees a small fraction of batch slots for high-priority/short cohorts and enforces dequeue fairness across cohorts with a decay-based crediting system.
3) KV rejuvenation TTL hints: when requests age beyond cohort thresholds, we emit lightweight KV 'rejuvenation' hints to avoid long-term pinning; a background scavenger can mark eligible pins for gentle eviction or rewarm.
4) Kernel path optimization for coalesced copies: adds an alias-safe fast-path that avoids an extra memcpy when building coalesced input tensors.
5) Timeouts/backoff tuning: jittered soft-timeout probe to detect stuck batches faster without aggressive preemption.

Bench results (perf-lab, kv-heavy synthetic trace):
- baseline: p50 12ms / p95 48ms / p99 210ms
- this PR: p50 13ms / p95 42ms / p99 118ms
- throughput: -2.8% at 99th percentile tail improvement.
- GPU utilization: +1.9% (better packing for background cohorts)

Notes on correctness and safety: cohort inference is conservative and can be overridden per-route; default cohorts preserve previous behavior. KV TTL hints are advisory; scavenger only acts when memory pressure > threshold to avoid unexpected evictions. The kernel fast-path is guarded by alias checks and has unit tests validating tensor semantics.

Tests and CI: added 28 new unit tests and 3 integration tests. CI: linux/unit, linux/integration, perf-lab run. One flaky test (kv_rejuv_integration_test) initially failed on CI due to timing; added retry and tightened assertions.
